claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has a multiphase microstructure consisting of a BCC solid solution and intermetallic phases.
The multiphase microstructure governs the plastic strain and toughness of WTaTiVZr at 800–1200°C.
The BCC solid-solution phase in WTaTiVZr enhances dislocation mobility and strain accommodation.
Intermetallic phases in WTaTiVZr impede crack propagation and cause crack deflection and energy dissipation.
Commercially pure polycrystalline tungsten is single-phase BCC.
Pure tungsten lacks the proposed dislocation-accommodation and crack-deflection mechanisms.
Pure tungsten fails by brittle cleavage under the specified high-temperature conditions.
WTaTiVZr will have higher plastic strain than pure tungsten under identical high-temperature testing conditions.
WTaTiVZr will have higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten under identical high-temperature testing conditions.
The plastic strain of WTaTiVZr is expected to be at least twice that of pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten is expected to exhibit less than 1–2% plastic strain under the proposed high-temperature test conditions.
The proposed comparison uses tensile or fracture-toughness testing of WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten under identical 800–1200°C vacuum or inert-atmosphere conditions.
The hypothesis is restricted to equimolar WTaTiVZr retaining a similar multiphase microstructure at 800–1200°C.
The hypothesis does not apply to off-stoichiometric WTaTiVZr, single-phase variants, or low-temperature conditions.
Direct experimental measurements of plastic strain and toughness in WTaTiVZr are lacking.
